chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Breaking up the big band
summary: Theaters and one-nighters dwindled, so in 1950 he cut down to hotel jobs and small groups.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. What were the circumstances, you know, surrounding, you know, your breaking up your big band?
Well, places like theatres The Fields began to close up. The one night stands, which used to be very good weren't like they used to be. A lot of places was closed.

So, it got to be kind of hard. So, I figured it was best. And then, the work began to, it wasn't as close together as it was before. We may play at the night, big band night, and then you'd have to wait for maybe 3 or 4 days before your next big job comes. Then, you'd have to ride, go 1,000 miles to it. And, I couldn't see it that way.

Then, I broke my big band down and it brought things closer. Then I started playing hotels something like two weeks, a month here, two weeks here, two months there, and I made things come closer to me. I played a lot of big hotels mainly through Canada. I played a lot in Canada, especially Toronto and Montreal.
So, I saw it better that way. It made it much easier for me. Then, I put the big band together when I needed it.
Right. When did you first break up the big band?
Sometime in '50. In late, the latter part of '50.
And, how large was it then?
17 pieces. And then, you broke it down. And you broke the smaller groups?
That was in '54, I think, you had the 7 pieces.
Right. Right. And then, finally when I, just a little before I came in here, I went to a quartet. You know, for a while, then, I came in and started with a quartet, split plus singer.
Finally, I added another piece, made it quartet (inaudible). Take some of the pressure off.
